title: Escort release traffic allocator and safety policy engine
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a new policy engine ("Escort") for orchestrating phased model introductions. Escort combines weighted traffic allocation, shadow probing, step-schedules, cohort-aware constraints, and automatic rollback triggers. This ticket covers the configuration schema, runtime policy evaluation, deterministic simulation harness, and console integration for visualization and manual overrides.
motivation: Current rollout tooling is brittle when traffic patterns vary by cohort (mobile vs web) and when backend latency spikes cause noisy telemetry. Escort aims to reduce blast radius, make progressive exposure predictable, and automate safe rollback decisions while making policies auditable in the Console.
goals: Design a human-readable policy DSL for multi-step rollouts with cohort splits and conditional gates
Implement runtime evaluator that can make allocation decisions per-request and persist state for step progress
Add shadow probing mode that mirrors a configurable percentage of traffic to new variant without affecting user-visible routing
Define automatic rollback criteria tied to SLO/quality contracts and implement a reversible rollback action
Expose rollout visualization and step controls in Redwood Console and provide API bindings
non_goals: Replacing existing low-level traffic router (we will integrate with current router)
Full A/B statistical engine for hypothesis testing (basic metrics only; detailed experiment infra is separate)
Implementing model retraining or evaluation pipelines (outside scope)
requirements: Policy DSL supports: fixed weights, linear ramps, wait-until-stable intervals, cohort selectors, shadow percentages, and rollback predicates
Runtime must evaluate policy in <2ms median additional latency per request on p95 serving path
State for rollout progress must be durable and showable in Console and via API
Rollback action must be atomic and revert traffic to last stable variant within 5 seconds of trigger
Telemetry hooks must emit per-step and per-cohort metrics (latency, error-rate, quality-regression)
design_summary: Escort uses a small declarative DSL (YAML/JSON) that compiles into an immutable policy object. At serving time, the policy evaluator consults request attributes (route, cohort tag, region) plus the current rollout state to compute a weighted decision and whether to shadow. A parallel simulation harness runs policies against historical traffic traces to estimate exposure curves. Rollback predicates are evaluated by the telemetry controller which compares streaming metric windows to thresholds and issues the rollback command to the orchestrator. Manual override endpoints exist for immediate cutover and for 'pause' to suspend schedule progression.
config_schema: Fields: name (string), steps (ordered list), each step: {duration: secs, target_weight: int 0-100, cohort_selector: expr, shadow_pct: 0-100, wait_for: [metrics predicates]}, initial_variant (string), stable_variant (string), fallback_policy: {max_failure_window, cooldown}. Example: {steps: [{duration: 3600, target_weight:5, cohort_selector: 'country!=CN', shadow_pct:10, wait_for:[ 'latency.p95<200', 'error_rate<0.01']}, ...]}
failure_modes: Noisy telemetry causes false positive rollback -> mitigate via hysteresis and multi-window checks
State store latency delays step progression -> degrade to conservative fixed weights
Policy misconfiguration that pins 100% traffic to new model -> require schema validation and preflight simulation
Shadow traffic causes downstream cost spike -> cap shadow spend and provide budget alerts
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL approved by PM and Design and documented in Console docs
End-to-end test: deploy a 3-step rollout for a dummy model; simulated traces show expected exposure curve within ±5%
Automatic rollback triggers on injected error-rate regressions in simulation and live can be validated in staging
Console UI shows per-step progress, provides pause/resume, and allows manual rollback within a single click
Latency overhead measured: median additional eval <2ms; p99 <10ms under typical load

api_considerations: Expose REST endpoints to create/validate/apply policies, query rollout state, and trigger manual actions. Policies are immutable once applied to a release token; updates create a new policy version. API supports dry-run simulation mode returning expected exposure timeline. Rate-limit management required on apply endpoints to prevent accidental mass changes.
console_note: Design should surface the active step, cohort exposure heatmap, and a time-slider showing historical progression. Provide 'simulate' button to run policy against sampled past traffic and display failure-mode warnings before apply.
security_notes: Policy apply requires RBAC permission 'rollout.manage'. Rollback and manual cutover actions must be audited with immutable logs. Ensure policy DSL cannot reference sensitive attributes (PII) in cohort selectors; only allow whitelisted request attributes.
deployment_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement evaluator and schema validation; run simulation on staging traces
Phase 2 (pilot): enable Escort for internal canary flows (internal models only) with 0.1% traffic
Phase 3 (opt-in customers): expose API and Console controls to a small set of customers; collect feedback
Phase 4 (general availability): harden performance, finalize docs, run security review
rollout_simulation_results: Initial simulation against last 7 days of trace shows Escort ramps to 20% of production traffic across step windows, with mean latency delta of +1.8ms and no quality regressions on baseline metrics. Simulated rollback on injected error spike restored exposure to stable_variant in <4s in 95% of trace segments.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly permissive cohort selectors -> Mitigation: sandboxed selector language + static analyzer
Risk: Telemetry gaps -> Mitigation: fallback metric hooks and conservative default behavior
Risk: Operator confusion in Console -> Mitigation: in-UI warnings, runbooks, and one-click abort
